lens: release safety and bump fit: uncloseable runs, false refusals, staged-analysis trust, and compatibility

target_observations.summary: The release contains useful additive controls, but the staged-tree proof can survive index drift, the coverage floor is not preserved by the durable delivered-report validator, and the body-chain migration can make previously valid live Goal Runs uncloseable. Shipping all three together as 8.8.0 is not yet safe.
evidence: scripts/gates_support/changed_line_run_trust.py: run_state_drift explicitly ignores HEAD movement for :staged: and compares only the worktree pool fingerprint; it never re-resolves and compares the staged index tree SHA pinned by probe_run_trust.

skills/shared/scripts/reviewer_worker_carrier_support.py: validate_delivered_worker_report calls _validate_delivery_chain without expected_targets, so its approval-independent durable validation does not enforce #819's declared target floor.

skills/public/issue/scripts/issue_goal_run_body_chain.py: an observed binding digest becomes a mandatory close anchor even when no body_revisions exist, while the prior contract allowed marker-preserving prose edits; there is no migration or grandfathering state for already-established runs.

findings.summary: A staged-tree verdict can be emitted after the staged index changes during the run, so the receipt need not describe the tree currently staged for commit.
evidence: probe_run_trust resolves git write-tree once and stores that tree as resolved_head_sha.
run_state_drift's STAGED_HEAD branch says a mid-run commit cannot invalidate analysis and checks only changed_pool_fingerprint, which is worktree-content based.
An index-only operation such as resetting or replacing a staged blob can change git write-tree while leaving worktree bytes and the pool fingerprint unchanged.
The staged tests cover worktree movement and ignored HEAD movement, but contain no test that changes the index tree while preserving worktree bytes.
findings.action: Pin the staged tree SHA and re-run git write-tree at finalization; mark the result untrusted if it differs. Add an index-only drift test. Also state whether non-pool execution inputs are intentionally outside the proof boundary.

findings.summary: The #819 floor is opt-in during collection but disappears at the durable delivered-worker validation boundary, allowing a schema-valid pass with null or incomplete target observations to be accepted as a delivered result.
evidence: validate_bounded_result enforces coverage only when expected_targets is supplied.
reviewer_runner_support.finalize_attempt and reviewer_worker_report.build_report can supply expected_targets.
validate_delivered_worker_report exposes no expected_targets argument and calls _validate_delivery_chain without one.
Its required report fields do not require coverage_ok or a cryptographically joined declaration of the expected target set.
findings.action: Bind the normalized expected-target set, or its digest, into the attempt/report provenance and require it again in validate_delivered_worker_report. Add an end-to-end test proving a thin pass cannot cross collection, promotion, and durable carrier validation.

findings.summary: The body-revision close guard retroactively tightens established runs that have an observed body digest but no revision chain, with no migration path for marker-preserving edits that were valid under the previous contract.
evidence: _accepted_body_digests always adds approved item observed.body_sha256, even when metadata.body_revisions is absent.
require_body_descent then requires the live body to match that digest whenever the accepted set is nonempty.
The module preserves marker-only behavior only for items with no recorded anchor; many reused items can have an observed digest.
A Goal Run established before 8.8.0 whose child prose was legitimately edited while retaining its marker can therefore refuse close after upgrade.
findings.action: Grandfather pre-chain runs explicitly or provide a verified migration operation that records the current live body as chain genesis before enforcing descent. Test a pre-8.8 established run with a marker-preserving body edit through closeout.

findings.summary: Record-first ordering protects against parent-record failure, but the child update lacks compare-and-swap protection and can overwrite a concurrent body change while recording a false supersession edge.
evidence: _update_managed_body reads the live child and hashes it as supersedes_sha256.
After the parent entry is written, tracker.update_issue_body is called for the child without expected_body_sha256 or an equivalent pre-write validator.
A concurrent child edit between those operations can be overwritten even though the recorded entry claims the submitted body superseded the earlier read body.
findings.action: Pass the read child digest as an expected pre-write digest and refuse/retry on mismatch. Add a test that mutates the child between parent recording and child update.

counterweight_triage.concern: Adding body_revisions to optional parent metadata is itself a major-version schema break.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The field is optional and validation accepts absence; the release blocker is the retroactive close behavior for observed digests, not the additive metadata field.

counterweight_triage.concern: The #819 target floor rejects legitimate target-free aggregation results.
counterweight_triage.disposition: expected_targets=None preserves target-free behavior. The issue is loss of the declared floor at a later durable validation boundary.

counterweight_triage.concern: Staged analysis necessarily refuses ordinary mid-work states.
counterweight_triage.disposition: Staged-only pool changes are accepted, unstaged pool changes receive an actionable staging remedy, and --allow-dirty remains advisory. Those refusals appear intentional; unchecked index drift is the material trust hole.

counterweight_triage.concern: The whole release requires a major version solely because controls became stricter.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The packet does not establish a major-version requirement for the additive CLI and review fields. If existing Goal Runs are grandfathered or migrated, these features fit a minor release; without that compatibility treatment, shipping the closeout change as a minor is unsafe.

next_move: Do not ship this packet as 8.8.0 yet. Fix staged-index drift, carry the #819 target declaration through durable validation, and add a compatibility/migration rule for pre-chain Goal Runs; then rerun bounded review with end-to-end regression evidence.
non_claims: No workspace state or tests outside the identity-bound inline payload were inspected.
This review does not claim the release requires a major version after the compatibility blockers are repaired.
This review does not assess issue text, commits, generated packaging artifacts, or behavior not represented in the supplied semantic input.
